standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial object and its product
standard_prerequisites.statement: A simplicial object of a category is a contravariant functor on the simplex category, and its product over an index set is computed degreewise when it exists.
standard_prerequisites.use: The product X is used degreewise throughout the proof (source lines 4910-4912, 4927-4940).

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy between morphisms of simplicial objects
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two morphisms of simplicial objects are homotopic when there is a family of maps in each degree satisfying the usual face and degeneracy identities expressing the homotopy.
standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma is about producing and extracting such families (source lines 4914-4924, 4927-4948).

standard_prerequisites.name: Canonical projections and finite products
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map into a product is determined by its components via the canonical projections, and a finite product can be manipulated degree by degree.
standard_prerequisites.use: Part (3) extracts the homotopies of the factors from a homotopy of the product maps using the projections (source lines 4920-4924, 4941-4948).

core_obligations: Package the factor homotopies: given homotopies from a_t to b_t for every t, construct a homotopy from the product map a to the product map b, by defining in each degree a map out of the product of the X_t whose components are the corresponding components of the factor homotopies (source lines 4927-4940).

Verify the homotopy identities: check that the constructed family satisfies the face and degeneracy identities defining a homotopy, component by component, using that the morphisms into a product are determined by their components (source lines 4930-4940).

Extract homotopies in the finite case: assuming T finite and a homotopy from a to b, produce for each t a homotopy from a_t to b_t by composing the given homotopy with the projections onto the factors, and conclude that part (1) follows from part (3) (source lines 4941-4948).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the product homotopy componentwise from the given factor homotopies.
Verify the homotopy identities componentwise via the projections.
In the finite case extract factor homotopies from a product homotopy and deduce part (1).

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-products-homotopy at source lines 4908-4925, three statements about products: finitely many homotopy equivalences between the factors give a homotopy equivalence of the products; a family of homotopies between the factor maps gives a homotopy between the product maps; and in the finite case the converse holds, namely a homotopy between the product maps gives homotopies between the factors. The proof at source lines 4927-4949 is a genuine write-out of the homotopy data. Part (2) has to package the given homotopies into a single homotopy between the product morphisms, which means carrying, in each degree, a map from the product of the X_t into the next degree of the product of the Y_t, and verifying the homotopy identity component by component. Part (3) is the converse and requires extracting from a homotopy between the product maps a homotopy for each factor, which uses that the finite product admits the canonical projections and that a map into a product is determined by its components; the finiteness hypothesis is what lets the extraction be carried out degree by degree. The statement lists the conclusions and none of the extraction or packaging argument. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
